basis: Neurodevelopmental/autonomic dysfunction and congenital contractures characterize disease; retinal degeneration affected 2/2 assessed survivors.

decisions.ocular: involved: early retinal degeneration in 2/2 assessed survivors ([series](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5005468/)).
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: congenital camptodactyly and joint contractures are characteristic structural features.

basis: Pancreatic neuroendocrine carcinoma maps to the endocrine pancreatic compartment; overlapping exocrine ancestry does not establish a separate exocrine component.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: neuroendocrine pancreatic differentiation supports endocrine classification; neither mixed exocrine differentiation nor direct exocrine dysfunction is established.

basis: Adrenal failure, myopathy and severe developmental delay define disease; potentially fatal megacystis 80-99%. Cap excludes intestinal abnormalities 80-99% and hepatic steatosis 30-79%.

decisions.neurologic: primary: severe psychomotor delay is explicitly defining; severe global developmental delay occurs in 80-99%, with seizures in 30-79%.

basis: Diabetes and optic atrophy define Wolfram; hearing loss ~60% and neurologic dysfunction ~50-60% in the broader syndrome. Subtype frequencies uncertain; urinary disease excluded at cap.

decisions.otologic: involved: progressive sensorineural hearing loss affects roughly 60% in Wolfram overall; diabetes and optic atrophy are the core diagnostic features.

basis: Congenital ocular motility impairment arises from cranial dysinnervation; brain malformations and neuropathy further support neurologic disease. Limb contractures are occasional.

decisions.neurologic: primary: developmental oculomotor nerve/nuclear abnormalities underlie CFEOM ([GeneReviews](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK1348/)).

basis: R. africae directly infects vascular endothelium, causing vasculitis; necrotic skin eschars occur in ~80-90% and represent tissue destruction rather than transient rash.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: endothelial infection causes dermal vasculitis ([histology](https://wwwnc.cdc.gov/eid/article/12/9/05-1540_article)).
decisions.dermatologic: involved: necrotic eschars occur in nearly all patients ([CDC](https://www.cdc.gov/ticks/media/pdfs/2025/03/tickborne-diseases-manual-508.pdf)).

basis: Structural congenital myopathy; ptosis causes eyelid dysfunction in 30-79%. Respiratory insufficiency occurs in only 1-4%; recurrent infections are separate diseases.

decisions.ocular: involved: myopathic ptosis represents direct loss of eyelid function in 30-79%; eyelids explicitly belong to the ocular axis.

basis: Platelet dysfunction, immunodeficiency and severe CNS impairment define HPS10; ocular albinism/nystagmus 1/1. Pulmonary interstitial abnormality 1/1 and cutaneous albinism excluded at cap.

decisions.pulmonary: none at cap: interstitial abnormality is reported in 1/1, but ocular dysfunction is more consistently established across HPS10; three other axes reflect severe defining disease.
decisions.ocular: involved: ocular albinism with nystagmus occurs in 1/1 annotated patients and impairs visual development; retained as the fourth axis.

basis: Sex cord-stromal tumors arise from gonadal endocrine/supporting lineages, including granulosa, theca, Sertoli and Leydig cells; hormone excess is not required for endocrine tumor origin.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: gonadal sex cord/stromal endocrine lineage establishes the axis; secretion is variable ([NCI](https://www.cancer.gov/publications/dictionaries/cancer-terms/def/sex-cord-gonadal-stromal-tumor)).

basis: Developmental impairment and limb defects define CDLS1; hearing loss ~85-90%, lacrimal stenosis 3/5. Reflux 25/40 is separately diagnosed; isolated hydronephrosis does not establish usual frequency.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: gastroesophageal reflux occurs in 25/40 but is usually diagnosed and coded as a separate disease; feeding symptoms alone do not establish direct GI damage.
decisions.otologic: involved: hearing impairment affects ~85-90%, with structural ear abnormalities ([consensus](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7136165/)).
